purpose: Passive source/access audit for pre-incident company exposure research.
method: 30 candidate onion addresses from community discovery lists and two source-owned Telegram bios; one official Tor Project control. Checks used the existing dark-mcp fetch_onion tool over stdio through Tor.

First-pass source requests used a 30-second total budget, with two concurrent fetches. Two important timeouts were retried with 60-second budgets and still failed. A timeout is a point-in-time collection failure, not a takedown verdict.

Three public forum homepages were separately inspected as HTML to locate exact section URLs. Seven selected section/thread pages were then tested through dark-mcp; two longer-timeout homepage retries brought follow-ups to nine.
Eight ordinary-web candidates were inspected separately for identity/access context. Those checks were not performed through the onion-only MCP tool and do not constitute forum collection.

Only observed public text and metadata were inspected. No registrations, logins, CAPTCHA solutions, payments, messages or credential tests were performed. No attachments were downloaded. A personal-record sample in one thread was removed from retained evidence.

Directory status is a lead, not identity or activity evidence. Mirrors are grouped into source families. Public homepage titles, last reply activity, original post time, incident date and collection time must remain distinct.

research_references.purpose: Historical cases show why access offers can precede later ransomware disclosure. Listings often omit victim names; this is not proof of an early OpenCode record.
Primary research establishes Exploit as an access-broker source; it does not grant this MCP access.
Explains competing forum successors and why brands/mirrors must not be conflated.
Regional relevance of the Portuguese-language forum.
Credential-market relevance and duplicate/recycled inventory limitations.
Access barriers and forum roles in the underground ecosystem.
Current API page labels unauthenticated v2 personal-use only; PRO requires a key and provides a business-use route subject to its terms. No key was created.
Primary maintainer repository for ransomware leak-site aggregation; it is supplementary disclosure coverage.
Officially published address for the successful Tor routing control.

counterfactual_assessment: No dated pre-disclosure OpenCode signal was established. This audit tests collection feasibility and source relevance, not historical completeness.

index_search_observations.note: Provider-index results are not live forum searches. The superagent.sh result is the same unrelated Natural News candidate seen in earlier tests, not verified exposure.
index_search_observations.sample_corpus: No OpenCode, superagent or LiteLLM matches in the small collected corpus; Claude matched the PwnForums homepage. These results do not establish absence.

next_collection_requirements: Forum-aware incremental collection of selected public sections, with pagination and original post/reply timestamps.
Explicit challenge/login/empty/partial states so an HTTP 200 page is not counted as discussion coverage.
Approved authenticated access or a licensed intelligence API for valuable gated sources; no access bypass.
A connector for ordinary-web forum mirrors, with the same provenance, access-state and pacing controls.
Source-level yield, original vs repost distinction and content deduplication.
Matching company domains/aliases plus contextual access-offer attributes; anonymous listings may omit the company name.
